name: Digital ceramic printing
summary: An inkjet printer puts ceramic ink onto a tile or a slab, with no contact. The print can show stone, wood or concrete and can change from tile to tile.
how: Make the image at 360 dpi or more.
Print with ceramic inks of metal oxides before the glost firing.
Vary the image over many tiles, so that no repeat shows.
Fire the tile so that the ink fuses to the glaze.

origin.note: Tile factories change from roller and screen printing to inkjet printing in the early 2000s.

adoptions.via: Italian and Spanish tile factories print stone and wood images on porcelain stoneware with ceramic inks.
